title: Catching up
goal: Catch up with a friend: say what you did at the weekend, what's new and what you've been up to, ask "have you ever…?", say what you were doing when something happened, and say how long ago or for how long.
intro:
Bumping into someone you haven't seen for ages is one of the best Nepali conversations to be able to handle — it starts with **भेट नभएको धेरै भयो!** 'long time no see!', moves quickly to remarks about how you've changed, and then to everybody's news: jobs, transfers, weddings, babies, someone who's gone to Korea or Australia.

The grammar is about time. You'll learn when Nepali uses the **perfect** (**गएको छु** 'I have been') instead of the simple past (**गएँ** 'I went'), the **past continuous** (**गर्दै थिएँ** 'I was doing'), and the very Nepali way of saying 'for' and 'since': नेपाल **आएको** दुई वर्ष **भयो** — literally 'since coming to Nepal, two years have become'.

vocab.note: Also आजभोलि and आजकल. अचेल के गर्दै छौ? 'what are you up to these days?'
Intransitive: तिमी फेरियौ 'you've changed'. To change something is फेर्नु.
From मोटो 'fat'. Said openly and usually kindly in Nepal.
From दुब्लो 'thin'. Often said with concern: बिरामी हुनुभयो कि?
थकाइ लाग्नु 'to feel tired' (experiencer): मलाई थकाइ लाग्यो.
The usual word in town. Nepal's weekend is traditionally Saturday only (plus Sunday in many offices since 2022).
ट्रिप जानु 'to go on a trip'. More formal: यात्रा, भ्रमण.
घुमघाम गर्नु. From घुम्नु.
अघिल्लो हप्ता 'the week before (last)'. Last week is गएको हप्ता; next week अर्को हप्ता.
A soft, everyday 'no', often with a shake of the head. Not for contradicting an elder.
Pokhara is one of the world's great paragliding spots.
राफ्टिङ जानु 'to go rafting' (the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi are the classic day trips).
पौडी खेल्नु 'to swim' (lit. 'play swimming').
कहिल्यै चाखेको छ? 'have you ever tried it?'
Also दगुर्नु. दौडन जानु 'to go for a run'.
With a -न verb: पढ्न थालेँ 'I started studying'. सुरु गर्नु is the noun-based equivalent.
कोर्स गर्नु 'to do a course'.
Written joined to the word before it: हिजोदेखि, सोमबारदेखि. After a verb: आएदेखि 'since coming'.

vocab.en: long ago, in the old days
vocab.note: Further back than उतिबेला 'back then'.
ड्राइभिङ सिक्नु 'to learn to drive'.
Getting one in Nepal means a written exam and a famously tough 'trial' on a figure-of-eight track.
Your personal news: के छ हालखबर? / हालखबर सुनाऊ न.
Government jobs and banks move staff around Nepal: मेरो सरुवा भयो 'I've been transferred'.
Also the Nepali term माग्नी or सगाई.
Past जन्म्यो (f जन्मी); also heard as जन्मियो. म पोखरामा जन्मेँ 'I was born in Pokhara'.
Degrees are usually named in English: ब्याचलर्स, मास्टर्स, पीएचडी.

phrases.note: Lit. 'it has become a long time since (we) didn't meet'.

phrases.en: Oh, you've put on weight, I see!
phrases.note: Fine between friends and from relatives; leave it out with people you don't know well.

phrases.en: What are you up to these days?
What did you do at the weekend?
Nothing special — I just stayed home.

phrases.note: In fast speech often गरेको छैन.

phrases.en: How long have you been in Nepal?

phrases.native: तिमीले फोन गर्दा म नुहाउँदै थिएँ।
phrases.roman: timile phon gardā ma nuhāuṃdai thieṃ.
phrases.en: When you called, I was in the shower.

grammar.title: Did or have done? The simple past and the perfect
grammar.body:
The **simple past** (unit 16) reports something that happened at a particular time: हिजो पोखरा **गएँ** 'I went to Pokhara yesterday'.

The **perfect** is the **-एको** participle + **छ**, and it talks about the past from the point of view of **now**:

म **गरेको छु** · हामी **गरेका छौँ**
तिमी **गरेका छौ** · ऊ **गरेको छ** (f **गरेकी छे**)
उनीहरू **गरेका छन्** · तपाईं **गर्नुभएको छ**

Transitive verbs keep their **ले**: **मैले** खाएको छु, **तपाईंले** गर्नुभएको छ. Negative: **-एको छैनँ / छैन / छैनौ…** (in speech usually just छैन).

Nepali uses the perfect mainly for:
**1. Experience** — 'have you ever…?' with **कहिल्यै** 'ever / never' and **पटक** 'times': तपाईं कहिल्यै राफ्टिङ **जानुभएको छ**? · म दुई पटक **गएको छु**.
**2. Not yet** — with **अझै / अहिलेसम्म**: अझै खाना **खाएको छैन**.
**3. News and present results**: मेरो सरुवा **भएको छ** 'I've been transferred'.

**The trap**: with a definite time (हिजो, गएको हप्ता, दुई दिन अघि) use the simple past, never the perfect. And where English says 'I've just eaten', Nepali is happy with the simple past: भर्खर **खाएँ**; 'have you eaten?' is **खाना खायौ?** or, very colloquially, **खाना खाएको?**

One step further back is the **past perfect -एको थियो** 'had done' — also used for anything in the more distant past: हामीले पहिले पनि **भेटेका थियौँ** 'we had met before'.

examples.native: म ठमेल धेरै पटक गएको छु।
examples.roman: ma Ṭhamel dherai paṭak gaeko chhu.
examples.en: I've been to Thamel lots of times.
Have you ever been to Chitwan?
I've never seen snow so far.

examples.native: हामीले पहिले पनि भेटेका थियौँ, होइन?
examples.roman: hāmile pahile pani bheṭekā thiyauṃ, hoina?

grammar.title: What were you doing? The past continuous
grammar.body:
For something that was **in progress** at a moment in the past, take the -दै form (unit 10) and add the past of छ, **थियो**:

म **गर्दै थिएँ** · हामी **गर्दै थियौँ**
तिमी **गर्दै थियौ** · ऊ **गर्दै थियो** (f **थिई**)
उनीहरू **गर्दै थिए** · तपाईं **गर्दै हुनुहुन्थ्यो**

Vowel stems nasalise: खाँदै, जाँदै, आउँदै, नुहाउँदै. The **-इरहेको थिएँ** form means the same with a stronger sense of 'right in the middle of': म सुतिरहेको थिएँ 'I was fast asleep'.

It's the background tense of stories, often paired with **-दा** 'when' (unit 20) or **अचानक** 'suddenly' for the event that interrupts: तिमीले फोन **गर्दा** म नुहाउँदै थिएँ 'when you called I was in the shower' · बाटोमा हिँड्दै थिएँ, **अचानक** पानी पर्‍यो 'I was walking along when suddenly it rained'.

The question everyone asks after a missed call: के **गर्दै थियौ**? 'what were you doing?'

**The trap**: don't confuse it with the 'used to' tense from unit 26: म खाना **खान्थेँ** 'I used to eat (habitually)' vs म खाना **खाँदै थिएँ** 'I was eating (at that moment)'.

examples.native: म अफिस जाँदै थिएँ, अचानक बाइक बिग्रियो।
examples.roman: ma aphis jāṃdai thieṃ, achānak bāik bigriyo.
examples.en: I was on my way to the office when suddenly my bike broke down.
I was fast asleep when you came.

examples.native: उनीहरू हिजो राति के गर्दै थिए?
examples.roman: uniharu hijo rāti ke gardai thie?
examples.en: What were they doing last night?

examples.native: बत्ती जाँदा हामी फिल्म हेर्दै थियौँ।
examples.roman: batti jāṃdā hāmi philm herdai thiyauṃ.
examples.en: We were watching a film when the power went.
What were you studying at that time?

grammar.title: Ago, since and for: अघि, -देखि, … भयो
grammar.body:
**Ago** — time + **अघि** (or **पहिले**): दुई दिन **अघि** 'two days ago', धेरै वर्ष **पहिले** 'many years ago'. Use the simple past with it.

**Since** — **-देखि** joined to the word: हिजो**देखि**, सोमबार**देखि**, पोहोर**देखि**. After a verb use **-एदेखि** 'since (doing)': नेपाल **आएदेखि** 'since I came to Nepal', बिहे **गरेदेखि** 'since getting married'.

**For (up to now)** — two everyday patterns:
• **time + देखि + present**: म दुई वर्ष**देखि** यहाँ बस्छु / बस्दै छु 'I've been living here for two years'.
• **verb-एको + time + भयो** 'it has been (time) since…' — the most Nepali way: नेपाल **आएको** दुई वर्ष **भयो** 'I've been in Nepal two years'; बिहे **भएको** पाँच वर्ष भयो 'we've been married five years'. Ask with **… कति भयो?** In the negative it means 'it's been X since I last…': भेट **नभएको** धेरै भयो 'it's been ages since we met'.

**For (a finished period)** — just the time, no word for 'for': म दुई वर्ष भारतमा बसेँ 'I lived in India for two years'.

**The trap**: English 'for' is **not** लागि here. **लागि** is only for a planned stay: दुई हप्ता**को लागि** आएँ 'I've come for two weeks'.

examples.native: म तीन दिन अघि काठमाडौं आएँ।
examples.roman: ma tin din aghi kāṭhmāḍauṃ āeṃ.
examples.en: I came to Kathmandu three days ago.

examples.native: काठमाडौं आएदेखि मैले पौडी खेलेको छैन।
examples.roman: kāṭhmāḍauṃ āedekhi maile pauḍi kheleko chhaina.
examples.en: I haven't been swimming since I came to Kathmandu.

examples.native: उनीहरूको बिहे भएको दस वर्ष भयो।
examples.roman: uniharuko bihe bhaeko das barsa bhayo.
examples.en: They've been married for ten years.

examples.native: म दुई हप्ताको लागि पोखरा जाँदै छु।
examples.roman: ma dui haptāko lāgi pokharā jāṃdai chhu.
examples.en: I'm going to Pokhara for two weeks.

dialogue.title: Three years later
dialogue.setting: Bibek bumps into his old school friend Suman at a momo place in Patan. They haven't seen each other since Suman went to work in Korea.

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: ए, बिबेक! भेट नभएको धेरै भयो!
lines.roman: e, Bibek! bheṭ nabhaeko dherai bhayo!
lines.en: Hey, Bibek! Long time no see!

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: सुमन! ओहो, कति वर्ष भयो? तिमी त धेरै फेरियौ नि!
lines.roman: Suman! oho, kati barsa bhayo? timi ta dherai pheriyau ni!
lines.en: Suman! Wow, how many years has it been? You've really changed!

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: तीन वर्ष भयो होला। तिमी चाहिँ अलि मोटाएछौ!
lines.roman: tin barsa bhayo holā. timi chāhiṃ ali moṭāechhau!
lines.en: Must be three years. And you've put on a bit of weight, I see!

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: बिहे गरेपछि सबै मोटाउँछन् नि! अनि, अचेल के गर्दै छौ?
lines.roman: bihe garepachhi sabai moṭāuṃchhan ni! ani, achel ke gardai chhau?
lines.en: Everyone gets fat after the wedding! So, what are you up to these days?

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: म दुई वर्ष कोरियामा काम गरेँ, गएको महिना मात्र फर्केँ।
lines.roman: ma dui barsa Koriyāmā kām gareṃ, gaeko mahinā mātra pharkeṃ.
lines.en: I worked in Korea for two years — I only got back last month.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.en: Really? How did you find Korea?

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: काम गाह्रो थियो, तर पैसा राम्रो थियो। अब यतै केही गर्ने विचार छ।
lines.roman: kām gāhro thiyo, tara paisā rāmro thiyo. aba yatai kehi garne bichār chha.
lines.en: The work was hard, but the money was good. Now I'm thinking of doing something here.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: राम्रो! तिमीले सुरजको खबर सुनेका छौ?
lines.roman: rāmro! timile Surajko khabar sunekā chhau?
lines.en: Good for you! Have you heard Suraj's news?

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: उसको त गएको हप्ता छोरा जन्म्यो रे!
lines.roman: usko ta gaeko haptā chhorā janmyo re!
lines.en: He had a baby boy last week, apparently!

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: बाबै! स्कुल पढ्दा ऊ त कक्षाको सबैभन्दा सानो थियो!
lines.roman: bābai! skul paḍhdā u ta kakchhāko sabaibhandā sāno thiyo!
lines.en: No way! At school he was the smallest kid in the class!

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: ल, नम्बर देऊ। अब भेट्दै गरौँ है!
lines.roman: la, nambar deu. aba bheṭdai garauṃ hai!
lines.en: Right, give me your number. Let's keep meeting up from now on!

culture:
Catching up in Nepal is warm and direct. Expect personal remarks — **मोटाएछौ!**, **दुब्लाएछौ!** — and personal questions: are you married yet, how much do you earn, when are you having children. You can deflect with a laugh and **खै, हेरौँ न** 'well, we'll see'. A classic greeting between acquaintances is **खाना खानुभयो?** 'have you eaten?' — it's a way of saying hello, not an invitation.

Almost every Nepali family has someone working or studying abroad — in the Gulf, Malaysia, Korea, Japan, Australia, the UK or the US — so **कहिले फर्कनुभयो?** 'when did you get back?' and **फेरि जाने?** 'are you going back?' are standard catching-up questions. **Dashain** is when people flood home from the cities and abroad, and the tea shops and family courtyards are full of exactly these conversations. Close friends end with a promise to meet more — **अब भेट्दै गरौँ** — and often an immediate plan for momo or tea.

tip.title: Noticing changes: -एछ
tip.body:
- When you **notice** something new, use the 'I see that…' form (unit 20): काठमाडौं फेरि**एछ** 'Kathmandu has changed!'
- To a friend: मोटा**एछौ**, दुब्ला**एछौ**. To तपाईं: दुब्लाउनु**भएछ**.
- For a state: तिमी त बिजी **रहेछौ** 'you're busy these days, I see'.

sentences.native: ओहो, तिमी त दुब्लाएछौ!
sentences.roman: oho, timi ta dublāechhau!
sentences.en: Wow, you've lost weight!

sentences.native: तपाईं त धेरै दुब्लाउनुभएछ, सन्चै हुनुहुन्छ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃ ta dherai dublāunubhaechha, sanchai hunuhunchha?
sentences.en: You've got very thin — are you keeping well?

sentences.native: बिहे गरेपछि ऊ मोटाएछ।
sentences.roman: bihe garepachhi u moṭāechha.
sentences.en: He's put on weight since getting married, I see.

sentences.native: तिम्रो कपाल छोटो भएछ, राम्रो छ!
sentences.roman: timro kapāl chhoṭo bhaechha, rāmro chha!
sentences.en: Your hair's short now — it looks good!

sentences.native: काठमाडौं त धेरै फेरिएछ!
sentences.roman: kāṭhmāḍauṃ ta dherai pheriechha!
sentences.en: Kathmandu has really changed!

sentences.native: तिमी त अचेल धेरै बिजी रहेछौ!
sentences.roman: timi ta achel dherai biji rahechhau!
sentences.en: You're really busy these days, I see!

sentences.native: अचेल धेरै थकाइ लाग्छ।
sentences.roman: achel dherai thakāi lāgchha.
sentences.en: I get really tired these days.

sentences.native: अचेल अफिसमा धेरै काम छ।
sentences.roman: achel aphismā dherai kām chha.
sentences.en: There's a lot of work at the office these days.

sentences.native: तिम्रो नयाँ जागिर कस्तो चल्दै छ?
sentences.roman: timro nayāṃ jāgir kasto chaldai chha?
sentences.en: How's the new job going?

lessons.title: What did you do at the weekend?

tip.title: Went or have been?
tip.body:
- A definite time (हिजो, विकेन्डमा, गएको हप्ता) → **simple past**: नगरकोट **गयौँ**.
- News or a result that matters now → **-एको छ**: नयाँ फोन किनेको **छु**.
- 'I've just…' is still the simple past: भर्खर **खाएँ**.
tip.pattern: time word + simple past  ·  news: -एको छु

sentences.native: विकेन्डमा हामी नगरकोट घुम्न गयौँ।
sentences.roman: wikenḍmā hāmi Nagarkoṭ ghumna gayauṃ.
sentences.en: We went to Nagarkot at the weekend.

sentences.native: शनिबार के गर्‍यौ?
sentences.roman: sanibār ke garyau?
sentences.en: What did you do on Saturday?

sentences.native: अघिल्लो विकेन्डमा साथीहरूसँग ट्रिप गएँ।
sentences.roman: aghillo wikenḍmā sāthiharusaṃga ṭrip gaeṃ.
sentences.en: The weekend before last I went on a trip with friends.

sentences.native: ट्रिप कस्तो भयो?
sentences.roman: ṭrip kasto bhayo?
sentences.en: How was the trip?

sentences.native: एकदम रमाइलो भयो, तर बाटोमा धेरै जाम थियो।
sentences.roman: ekdam ramāilo bhayo, tara bāṭomā dherai jām thiyo.
sentences.en: Really fun, but there was loads of traffic on the way.

sentences.native: मैले भर्खर नयाँ फोन किनेको छु, हेर!
sentences.roman: maile bharkhar nayāṃ phon kineko chhu, hera!
sentences.en: I've just bought a new phone — look!

sentences.native: दसैंको बिदामा कतै घुमघाम गर्‍यौ?
sentences.roman: dasaiṃko bidāmā katai ghumghām garyau?
sentences.en: Did you go off travelling anywhere in the Dashain holiday?

sentences.native: हिजो राति कहाँ गएका थियौ? फोन उठाएनौ नि।
sentences.roman: hijo rāti kahāṃ gaekā thiyau? phon uṭhāenau ni.
sentences.en: Where had you got to last night? You didn't pick up.

sentences.native: म दिनभरि सुतेँ, कतै गइनँ।
sentences.roman: ma dinbhari suteṃ, katai gainaṃ.
sentences.en: I slept all day — didn't go anywhere.

sentences.native: अर्को विकेन्ड घुमघाम गर्न कतै जाऔँ न।
sentences.roman: arko wikenḍ ghumghām garna katai jāauṃ na.
sentences.en: Let's go off somewhere next weekend.

tip.title: Ever, never, not yet: -एको छ
tip.body:
- **कहिल्यै + -एको छ?** 'have you ever…?': तपाईं कहिल्यै राफ्टिङ **जानुभएको छ**?
- Yes: दुई पटक **गएको छु**. No: अहँ, कहिल्यै **गएको छैनँ**.
- With तिमी: **गएका छौ**; with ले-verbs keep ले: **मैले** चाखेको छु.
- 'Not yet': **अझै** खाएको **छैन**.

sentences.native: तपाईं कहिल्यै राफ्टिङ जानुभएको छ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃ kahilyai rāphṭiṅ jānubhaeko chha?
sentences.en: Have you ever been rafting?

sentences.native: मैले दुई पटक प्याराग्लाइडिङ गरेको छु।
sentences.roman: maile dui paṭak pyārāglāiḍiṅ gareko chhu.
sentences.en: I've been paragliding twice.

sentences.native: तिमीले कहिल्यै खसीको मासु चाखेका छौ?
sentences.roman: timile kahilyai khasiko māsu chākhekā chhau?
sentences.en: Have you ever tried goat meat?

sentences.native: अहँ, अहिलेसम्म चाखेको छैनँ।
sentences.roman: ahaṃ, ahilesamma chākheko chhainaṃ.
sentences.en: Nope, I haven't tried it yet.

sentences.native: म कहिल्यै हवाईजहाजमा चढेको छैनँ।
sentences.roman: ma kahilyai hawāijahājmā chaḍheko chhainaṃ.
sentences.en: I've never been on a plane.

sentences.native: तपाईंले कहिल्यै पोखराको तालमा पौडी खेल्नुभएको छ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃle kahilyai pokharāko tālmā pauḍi khelnubhaeko chha?
sentences.en: Have you ever swum in the lake at Pokhara?

sentences.native: म नेपाल पाँच पटक आएको छु।
sentences.roman: ma nepāl pāṃch paṭak āeko chhu.
sentences.en: I've been to Nepal five times.

sentences.native: तपाईंले नेपाली खाना पकाउन सिक्नुभएको छ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃle nepāli khānā pakāuna siknubhaeko chha?
sentences.en: Have you learned to cook Nepali food?

sentences.native: मैले अझै भात खाएको छैनँ, भोक लाग्यो।
sentences.roman: maile ajhai bhāt khāeko chhainaṃ, bhok lāgyo.
sentences.en: I still haven't had my dal bhat — I'm starving.

sentences.native: राफ्टिङ एक पटक त गर्नैपर्छ!
sentences.roman: rāphṭiṅ ek paṭak ta garnaiparchha!
sentences.en: You've got to go rafting at least once!

lessons.title: What were you doing?

tip.title: Was doing: -दै थिएँ
tip.body:
- -दै + **थियो**: म गर्दै **थिएँ**, हामी गर्दै **थियौँ**, तिमी गर्दै **थियौ**, ऊ गर्दै **थियो**, तपाईं गर्दै **हुनुहुन्थ्यो**.
- 'Right in the middle of': **-इरहेको थिएँ**: सुतिरहेको थिएँ.
- The interruption: **-दा** 'when' or **अचानक** 'suddenly'.
- Not the 'used to' form: खान्थेँ ≠ खाँदै थिएँ.

new: तिमीले फोन गर्दा म नुहाउँदै थिएँ।

sentences.native: हिजो बेलुका सात बजे के गर्दै थियौ?
sentences.roman: hijo belukā sāt baje ke gardai thiyau?
sentences.en: What were you doing at seven last night?

sentences.native: म जिममा दौडिरहेको थिएँ।
sentences.roman: ma jimmā dauḍiraheko thieṃ.
sentences.en: I was running at the gym.

sentences.native: फोन आउँदा म सुतिरहेको थिएँ।
sentences.roman: phon āuṃdā ma sutiraheko thieṃ.
sentences.en: I was asleep when the phone rang.

sentences.native: अचेल म बिहान दौडन थालेको छु।
sentences.roman: achel ma bihāna dauḍana thāleko chhu.
sentences.en: I've started running in the mornings these days.

sentences.native: पोहोर म नेपाली भाषाको कोर्स गर्दै थिएँ।
sentences.roman: pohor ma nepāli bhāsāko kors gardai thieṃ.
sentences.en: Last year I was doing a Nepali course.

sentences.native: म बसमा थिएँ, त्यसैले फोन उठाइनँ।
sentences.roman: ma basmā thieṃ, tyasaile phon uṭhāinaṃ.
sentences.en: I was on the bus, so I didn't pick up.

sentences.native: बाटोमा हिँड्दै थिएँ, अचानक पानी पर्‍यो।
sentences.roman: bāṭomā hiṃḍdai thieṃ, achānak pāni paryo.
sentences.en: I was walking down the road when suddenly it started raining.

sentences.native: तिमी आउँदा हामी खाना खाँदै थियौँ।
sentences.roman: timi āuṃdā hāmi khānā khāṃdai thiyauṃ.
sentences.en: We were eating when you arrived.

sentences.native: उनीहरू के कुरा गर्दै थिए?
sentences.roman: uniharu ke kurā gardai thie?
sentences.en: What were they talking about?

sentences.native: तपाईं उतिबेला कहाँ काम गर्दै हुनुहुन्थ्यो?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃ utibelā kahāṃ kām gardai hunuhunthyo?
sentences.en: Where were you working back then?

sentences.native: तिमी जिम कति बजे जान्छौ?
sentences.roman: timi jim kati baje jānchhau?
sentences.en: What time do you go to the gym?

tip.title: Ago, since, for
tip.body:
- **Ago**: दुई वर्ष **अघि**.
- **Since**: हिजो**देखि**; after a verb **-एदेखि**: लाइसेन्स पा**एदेखि**.
- **For (until now)**: verb-**एको** + time + **भयो**: नेपाल आएको तीन महिना **भयो**. Ask: **कति भयो?**
- 'For' here is never लागि.

sentences.native: नेपाल आएको तीन महिना भयो।
sentences.roman: nepāl āeko tin mahinā bhayo.
sentences.en: I've been in Nepal for three months.

sentences.native: कहिलेदेखि नेपाली सिक्दै छौ?
sentences.roman: kahiledekhi nepāli sikdai chhau?
sentences.en: How long have you been learning Nepali?

sentences.native: म पोहोरदेखि नेपाली सिक्दै छु।
sentences.roman: ma pohordekhi nepāli sikdai chhu.
sentences.en: I've been learning Nepali since last year.

sentences.native: दुई वर्ष अघि हामीले पहिलो पटक भेटेका थियौँ।
sentences.roman: dui barsa aghi hāmile pahilo paṭak bheṭekā thiyauṃ.
sentences.en: We first met two years ago.

sentences.native: उहिले यहाँ यति धेरै गाडी थिएनन्।
sentences.roman: uhile yahāṃ yati dherai gāḍi thienan.
sentences.en: In the old days there weren't this many cars here.

sentences.native: ड्राइभिङ सिक्न थालेको एक महिना भयो।
sentences.roman: ḍrāibhiṅ sikna thāleko ek mahinā bhayo.
sentences.en: It's been a month since I started learning to drive.

sentences.native: लाइसेन्स पाएदेखि म बाइक मात्र चलाउँछु।
sentences.roman: lāisens pāedekhi ma bāik mātra chalāuṃchhu.
sentences.en: Since I got my licence I only ride my motorbike.

sentences.native: हाम्रो भेट नभएको कति भयो होला?
sentences.roman: hāmro bheṭ nabhaeko kati bhayo holā?
sentences.en: How long has it been since we last met, d'you reckon?

sentences.native: लगभग पाँच वर्ष भयो जस्तो लाग्छ।
sentences.roman: lagbhag pāṃch barsa bhayo jasto lāgchha.
sentences.en: Must be about five years, I think.

sentences.native: म दुई वर्ष भारतमा बसेँ, अनि नेपाल आएँ।
sentences.roman: ma dui barsa Bhāratmā baseṃ, ani nepāl āeṃ.
sentences.en: I lived in India for two years, and then came to Nepal.

sentences.native: अनि, तिम्रो हालखबर सुनाऊ न!
sentences.roman: ani, timro hālkhabar sunāu na!
sentences.en: So — tell me your news!

sentences.native: दिदीको इन्गेजमेन्ट भयो, अर्को महिना बिहे!
sentences.roman: didiko ingejmenṭ bhayo, arko mahinā bihe!
sentences.en: My sister got engaged — the wedding's next month!

sentences.native: तिम्रो सरुवा कहाँ भयो?
sentences.roman: timro saruwā kahāṃ bhayo?
sentences.en: Where have you been transferred to?

sentences.native: मेरो काठमाडौं सरुवा भयो, अब हामी धेरै भेट्छौँ!
sentences.roman: mero kāṭhmāḍauṃ saruwā bhayo, aba hāmi dherai bheṭchhauṃ!
sentences.en: I've been transferred to Kathmandu — we'll see loads of each other now!

sentences.native: दाइको छोरा जन्म्यो!
sentences.roman: dāiko chhorā janmyo!
sentences.en: My brother's had a baby boy!

sentences.native: बधाई छ! छोरा कि छोरी?
sentences.roman: badhāi chha! chhorā ki chhori?
sentences.en: Congratulations! A boy or a girl?

sentences.native: तिम्रो मास्टर्स सकियो?
sentences.roman: timro māsṭars sakiyo?
sentences.en: Have you finished your Master's?

sentences.native: अँ, गएको महिना सकियो, अब जागिर खोज्दै छु।
sentences.roman: aṃ, gaeko mahinā sakiyo, aba jāgir khojdai chhu.
sentences.en: Yes, finished last month — now I'm looking for a job.

sentences.native: ऊ मास्टर्स पढ्न अमेरिका गएको छ।
sentences.roman: u māsṭars paḍhna Amerikā gaeko chha.
sentences.en: He's gone to America to do a Master's.

sentences.native: इन्गेजमेन्ट कहिले हो?
sentences.roman: ingejmenṭ kahile ho?
sentences.en: When's the engagement?
